title: Split torus weights of a finite locally free module over any ring
statement: Let $A$ be any commutative ring and $M=\mathbf Z^r$ for $r\geq0$. Let $A[M]$ have basis $e^m$ for $m\in M$, multiplication $e^me^n=e^{m+n}$, coproduct $e^m\mapsto e^m\otimes e^m$ and counit $e^m\mapsto1$. Let $V$ be a finite projective $A$-module, meaning a direct summand of a finite free module, with $A$-linear coaction $\rho:V\to V\otimes_A A[M]$ satisfying coassociativity and counitality. Put $V_m=\{v\in V:\rho(v)=v\otimes e^m\}$. Then the sum map $\bigoplus_{m\in M}V_m\to V$ is an isomorphism; only finitely many $V_m$ are nonzero and each is finite projective. For every ring map $A\to A'$ one has $(V\otimes_A A')_m=V_m\otimes_A A'$ under the natural inclusions. For a subgroup $L\subseteq M$ with $M/L$ free, restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}A[M/L]\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$ has invariant module $\bigoplus_{m\in L}V_m$, again compatibly with arbitrary base change [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. At every $s\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, an open neighborhood exists on which all the fibre dimensions $\dim_{\kappa(u)}(V_m\otimes_A\kappa(u))$, with $\kappa(u)$ the residue field [def-weil-residue-field], are equal to their values at $s$. The zero ring and $V=0$ are allowed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf . Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), printed pp.86-87, paragraph beginning with the T-action on the vector bundle g; Lemma 2.2.4 proof, printed p.66, group-algebra grading. General algebraic formulation over an arbitrary ring; local rank constancy is the finite-projective rank theorem.

proof.text: For any $A$-module $W$, define $c_m:W\otimes_A A[M]\to W$ on pure tensors by $c_m(w\otimes\sum_n a_ne^n)=a_mw$. This is balanced and additive, so is defined by the tensor-product relations. The map $\bigoplus_M W\to W\otimes_A A[M]$, $(w_m)\mapsto\sum_m w_m\otimes e^m$, has inverse $z\mapsto(c_m(z))_m$: a tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so the latter family has finite support, and both composites are the identity by expanding the finitely supported coefficients. The identical construction works with two group-algebra factors. Thus coefficient comparison is valid over every ring, without a domain or flatness assumption.

proof.text: Put $p_m=c_m\rho$. Write $\rho(v)=\sum_n p_n(v)\otimes e^n$. Applying $1\otimes1\otimes\operatorname{coeff}_m$ to $(\rho\otimes1)\rho(v)=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho(v)$ gives $\rho(p_m(v))=p_m(v)\otimes e^m$. Hence $p_m(v)\in V_m$. Counitality gives $v=\sum_m p_m(v)$. If $w\in V_n$, applying $c_m$ to $\rho(w)=w\otimes e^n$ gives $p_m(w)=\delta_{mn}w$; in particular $p_m^2=p_m$ and $p_mp_n=0$ for $m\ne n$.

proof.text: The inverse to the sum map is $v\mapsto(p_m(v))_m$, with finite support by step 1. Its composite with the sum map is the identity by counitality, and the other composite is the identity by $p_m|_{V_n}=\delta_{mn}$. This proves precisely the asserted internal direct sum.

proof.text: Choose split maps $i:V\to A^N$ and $q:A^N\to V$ with $qi=1$, available by the stated meaning of finite projective. The vectors $v_j=q(e_j)$ generate $V$. Let $F$ be the union of the finite supports of the families $(p_m(v_j))_m$ for $1\le j\le N$. If $m\notin F$, linearity gives $p_m=0$, whence $V_m=0$ because $p_m$ is the identity there. This includes $N=0$ and the empty set $F$.

proof.text: For each $m$, let $r_m:V\to V_m$ be $p_m$ with its codomain restricted, and let $j_m:V_m\to V$ be inclusion. Then $r_mj_m=1$. The maps $ij_m:V_m\to A^N$ and $r_mq:A^N\to V_m$ compose to $1_{V_m}$. Explicitly $A^N=ij_m(V_m)\oplus\ker(r_mq)$: write $x=ij_mr_mq(x)+(x-ij_mr_mq(x))$; intersection zero follows by applying $r_mq$. Thus each $V_m$ is a direct summand of a finite free module, exactly the finite-projectivity required.

source.place: WANTED locally; author PDF https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf read online: Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), printed pp.86-87, weight-bundle paragraph; Lemma 2.2.4 proof, printed p.66. Explicit coefficient arguments supplied by Q06.

proof.text: Let $A\to A\prime$ be arbitrary. Write $V\prime=V\otimes_A A\prime$ with its scalar-extended coaction and identify $A[M]\otimes_A A\prime=A\prime[M]$ by $e^m\otimes a\prime\mapsto a\prime e^m$, whose inverse sends $a\prime e^m$ to $e^m\otimes a\prime$. On pure tensors the coefficient projections satisfy $p\prime_m(v\otimes a\prime)=p_m(v)\otimes a\prime$. The map $j_m\otimes1$ is injective since $r_m\otimes1$ is a left inverse. Its image is $\operatorname{im}(p_m\otimes1)$, since $p_m=j_mr_m$ and $p_mj_m=j_m$. The calculation of step 2 over $A\prime$ identifies this image with $(V\prime)_m$. This proves the claimed equality under the natural inclusions; no preservation of arbitrary kernels by tensor is asserted.

source.place: WANTED locally; author PDF https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf read online: Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), printed pp.86-87, weight-bundle paragraph; Lemma 2.2.4 proof, printed p.66. Explicit coefficient arguments supplied by Q06.

proof.text: For restriction to the indicated subgroup use the explicit quotient Hopf map $A[M]\to A[M/L]$, $e^m\mapsto e^{\bar m}$. The restricted coaction of $v=\sum_m v_m$ is $\sum_m v_m\otimes e^{\bar m}$. Invariants mean that this equals $v\otimes e^0$. Comparing coefficients as in step 1 gives $\sum_{\bar m=b}v_m=0$ for every $b\ne0$. Applying $p_n$ to this equality gives $v_n=0$ for every $n\notin L$. Conversely every $v_m$ with $m\in L$ is invariant. Thus the invariant module is $\bigoplus_{m\in L}V_m$. Its inclusion splits by $\sum_{m\in F\cap L}p_m$; after any base change step 6 identifies its summands with the same weights over $A\prime$, proving base-change compatibility. Only the given Hopf map and the coaction definition of invariants are needed; no group of $A$-points is substituted for the group scheme.

source.place: WANTED locally; author PDF https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf read online: Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), printed pp.86-87, weight-bundle paragraph; Lemma 2.2.4 proof, printed p.66. Explicit coefficient arguments supplied by Q06.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-rank-locally-constant] to each of the finite-projective modules $V_m$ for $m\in F$. For a prime $u$, a free basis of $(V_m)_u$ reduces to a basis over $\kappa(u)=A_u/uA_u$, the residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ at $u$ [def-weil-residue-field] identified with that of $A_u$ by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field], and $V_m\otimes_A\kappa(u)=(V_m)_u\otimes_{A_u}\kappa(u)$, so its local rank is exactly $\dim_{\kappa(u)}(V_m\otimes_A\kappa(u))$. At a fixed $s$, intersect the finitely many open neighborhoods on which these ranks equal their values at $s$. All $m\notin F$ give the zero module and rank zero everywhere, so this one neighborhood works for every $m$. If $F$ is empty take all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; if $A$ is the zero ring its spectrum is empty and this last assertion is vacuous.
